requests.title: 船舶动力
requests.prompt:
Edit the supplied harbor image into ONE landscape game environment art-direction prototype. Preserve the original viewpoint, spatial composition, stepped wet stone river embankment, old warehouse buildings on the left, inviting amber-lit interiors, open broad river on the right, foreground working barge, rainy blue-grey dusk, and everyday human scale. Strong Fallen Aces inspired noir graphic-novel game aesthetic: confidently inked edges, broad painted shadow shapes, hand-painted textured simple 3D architectural forms, readable normal human figures treated like 2D illustrated sprites. Atmospheric, inhabited, appealing and immersive. Keep ordinary dockworkers in plain period workwear, including the red-jacket courier. Original fictional river port architecture, familiar and believable. Art direction is 90 percent grounded old harbor noir and just 10 percent restrained practical retro science-fiction / steam-electric engineering. All added machines serve clear modest everyday port functions. Do not turn this into fantasy, mysticism, horror, a temple, or a robot world. No masks, robes, cult motifs, humanoid machine faces, ivory eggs, giant machinery, gear decoration, brass overload, Victorian goggles, or neon cyberpunk. Maintain open navigable steps and landing, mundane ropes, crates, rainwear, lamps, weathered wood and stone. STRICT ABSOLUTE ZERO TEXT ANYWHERE: remove all original calligraphy and writing from walls, banners, flags, boats and crates; remove clock numbers; no letters, digits, pseudo-writing, labels, logos, symbols resembling script, watermark, interface or caption. Replace signs with plain weathered surfaces, and use a simple unnumbered clock dial if retained. The image should remain an environment view, not a product closeup.
VARIANT A — quietly advanced working boat. Main distinctive addition on the foreground right barge: a compact rounded charcoal-painted engine housing partly tucked under the existing canopy, a small protected amber-glowing glass cylinder, two short insulated pipes and a low exhaust giving a thin wisp of steam. Build it as restrained 1940s industrial-design retrofuturism, with large simple casings, believable bolted panels and only small worn copper details. Its warm engine glow subtly catches wet deck planks and nearby water. A worker casually checks the engine. Preserve the boat's low silhouette and wooden working character; no towering boiler or huge exposed flywheel. Architecture remains almost identical to reference. Make the boat landing feel like somewhere one wants to step aboard.
